Panorama engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Panorama rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app wide-stitch capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Panorama mode — Apple Camera feature that captures wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while the user pans the phone along a guided arrow. Labeled 全景, 全景照片, or 全景模式 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • Frame stitching & sweep alignment — computational alignment that merges successive frames into one ultra-wide image as the phone moves. Your listing may mention wide stitch or panoramic photo; building stitching pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Gyro-guided panning UI — arrow overlay, speed hints, and vertical-vs-horizontal orientation switching in the viewfinder. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; panorama sample photo production is outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVFoundation & capture sessions — camera session code that reads frames during a sweep and drives the panorama viewfinder. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Panorama value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Panorama support in the binary.

A working Panorama story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Panorama vs Cinematic Mode vs Portrait Mode vs Live Photos vs Night Mode vs Macro vs Action Mode vs Photographic Styles — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge nine Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Panorama — wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while panning the phone — not cinematic video blur, not portrait background blur, not motion stills, not low-light modes, not macro close-ups, not video stabilization, and not tone presets:

  • Panorama & wide stitch stills (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Panorama", "Panorama mode", "Panoramic photo", "Wide stitch", "Sweep capture", "Horizontal panorama", "Vertical panorama", 全景, 全景照片, 全景模式, 横向全景, 纵向全景. Ultra-wide stitched still photos captured while panning the phone.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not still-photo panorama sweeps.
  • Portrait Mode listing copy (different) — shallow depth-of-field still photography with soft background blur: Portrait Mode, 人像模式, 景深虚化, 背景虚化. Subject-background separation — not ultra-wide stitched landscapes. Covered on our Portrait Mode guide.
  • Live Photos listing copy (different) — still photos with a few seconds of motion before and after the shutter: Live Photos, 实况照片, 动态照片. Motion stills — not wide stitch panorama marketing.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light photography — not daytime skyline panorama sweeps.
  • Macro listing copy (different) — extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance: Macro, Macro Control, 微距, 微距近拍. Close-up detail shots — not wide horizontal stitches. Covered on our Macro guide.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖. Video stabilization — not still-photo panorama capture. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, Rich Contrast, Vibrant, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Photo color grading — not wide stitch framing. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.
  • Burst, Time-Lapse, and Slo-Mo (different) — rapid still burst, time-lapse video compression, and slow-motion video are separate Camera modes with different screenshot vocabulary — not Panorama wide-stitch still marketing.

Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on stills. Live Photos adds motion around a still. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Action Mode stabilizes handheld video. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Panorama-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Wide-stitch listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Panorama feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Panorama phrasing

US pages use "Panorama", "Panorama mode", "Panoramic photo", "Wide stitch", "Sweep capture", or "Capture ultra-wide views." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 全景 for the general feature, 全景照片 for panoramic photo marketing, and 全景模式 for the Camera mode toggle. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing panorama capabilities your app does not support.

Horizontal vs vertical sweeps

Panorama marketing often shows left-to-right skyline sweeps or top-to-bottom interior tall shots. Chinese buyers expect concise labels: 横向全景 for horizontal panorama, 纵向全景 for vertical panorama — not English "Pan left" or "Pan up" pasted through machine translation without context.

Guided arrow and sweep UI

Screenshot overlays differ by step — mode picker, arrow alignment, mid-sweep progress bar, finished ultra-wide output. Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 全景模式 for the toggle, 跟随箭头移动 for follow-the-arrow guidance, 拼接完成 for stitched output — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Do not conflate with Portrait Mode, Cinematic Mode, or Macro

Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on still photos. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Macro captures extreme close-ups at minimum focus distance. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need panorama search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 全景, 全景照片, and 全景模式 each signal different intent from Portrait Mode 人像模式 keywords or Macro 微距 keywords.

How is this different from Cinematic Mode, Portrait Mode, Live Photos, Night Mode, Macro, Action Mode, or Photographic Styles?

Panorama copy markets wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while panning the phone — 全景, 全景照片, 全景模式. Cinematic Mode copy markets shallow-depth cinematic video — 浅景深电影效果视频. Portrait Mode copy markets background blur on stills — 人像模式, 景深虚化. Live Photos copy markets motion stills — 实况照片. Night Mode copy markets low-light capture — 夜间模式. Macro copy markets extreme close-ups — 微距, 微距近拍. Action Mode copy markets handheld video stabilization — 动作模式, 运动防抖. Photographic Styles copy markets still-photo tone presets — 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Caption and overlay fields are managed per localization. If you filled en-US screenshot text but never saved zh-Hans caption lines — or uploaded the same English-overlay PNGs to the Chinese set — China buyers see Latin Panorama badges on the product page.

Each appears in Chinese storefront and search contexts. AppLocale picks phrasing that matches your English listing claims and screenshot overlays — 全景 for the general feature, 全景照片 for panoramic photo marketing, 全景模式 for the Camera mode toggle — without inventing capabilities your app does not support.
